entities.name: DnaK Hsp70
observations: The 634-residue sequence is an exact sequence match to reviewed UniProt reference Q3A8C2, annotated as bacterial chaperone protein DnaK.
Pfam detects an HSP70 domain spanning residues 4–598 with i-Evalue 9.1e-279.
The N-terminal region begins with the characteristic DnaK/Hsp70 ATPase signature GIDLGTTNSC.
Curated homolog annotations support ATP binding, ATP hydrolysis, cytoplasmic localization, and protein folding.
The sequence is highly acidic overall: predicted pI 4.78 and charge at pH 7 approximately -32.8; these are sequence-derived estimates.

entities.name: Hsp70 ATPase domain
observations: The N-terminal DnaK nucleotide-binding domain contains conserved P-loop-like Hsp70 motifs and is responsible for ATP binding and hydrolysis.
The sequence includes the conserved N-terminal GIDLGTTNSC motif characteristic of the Hsp70/DnaK family.

entities.name: DnaK substrate-binding domain
observations: The C-terminal half of bacterial DnaK is the substrate-binding region, followed by a flexible glycine-rich lid/tail that regulates access to bound unfolded polypeptides.
The sequence architecture is consistent with a full-length bacterial DnaK rather than a truncated Hsp70 domain.

entities.name: Protein folding
observations: Reviewed DnaK homologs are annotated with GO:0006457 protein folding and GO:0005737 cytoplasm.
